title: Applying Payments and Refunds Across Entry & Patio Door Contracts
content:
Every payment toward Entry & Patio Door Contracts is applied to exactly one door contract and is never split across contracts.

## Where a payment is applied

1. The payment goes to the contract whose contract number the customer gives.
2. When the customer names no contract and holds more than one open door contract, it goes to the open door contract with the earliest signed date that still has a balance due.
3. A payment intended for a window contract is never booked to a door contract.
4. Lender funding is applied to the contract named on the funded financing account.

An open door contract here is one in status signed, measured, ordered or installed.

## Refunds follow their payment

A refund is always booked against the same door contract as the payment it returns and names that payment as its source. The source payment and the door contract it was booked to are read from the company's payment records, not from the customer's description of the payment.

| Element of a refund | Fixed by |
|---|---|
| The door contract it is booked against | The door contract of the payment it returns |
| The source it names | That payment |

## Applying the clauses (hypothetical customers)

- A customer pays and quotes contract number D-1001. The whole payment is applied to that contract, even if the customer holds a second open door contract.
- A customer holds two open door contracts, one signed in March and one signed in May, both with a balance due, and names no contract. The payment goes to the March contract in full; no part of it goes to the May contract.
- The same customer's March contract has no balance due and the May contract does. With no contract named, the payment goes to the May contract, which is the earliest-signed open door contract that still has a balance due.
- A customer sends money meant for a Ridgeline window contract. It is not booked to any door contract.
- A refund of part of a card payment that was booked to contract D-1001 is booked against D-1001 and names that card payment as its source.
